conviction_note: No unpriced fundamental was found: every pipeline, financing and NAV item is already on the wire, and the enormous discount to a readily-marked NAV (PureTech-level cash $248.1m at 31 Mar 2026 plus 16.68m Seaport/SPTX shares worth ~$356m today, against a ~245.2m-share, 121.0p, ~$400m market cap) is the oldest and most-discussed fact about this company. What the two passes did turn up is a reaction function that is currently hostile -- the last three scheduled results prints returned -2.23%, -5.52% and -4.15%, and on 21 September the company put out a positive FDA Fast Track / End-of-Phase-1 RNS at 07:01, traded to 127.0p and closed at 121.0p, the low of the day -- set against one genuinely under-read domestic fact, Tang Capital's move to 6.07% on 25 August, which raises the odds of a capital-return statement at the interims and truncates the downside. Sum of findings is -0.8; I emit -0.6 because the sealed lean is +1.25 and a 6%-plus sub-NAV activist on the register is a floor, so the caveat is taken out of the number rather than left in prose.
bar: No meaningful EPS consensus exists for a 4-analyst holding company; the bar is the company's own guidance -- operational runway at least through end-2028, PureTech-level cash and cash equivalents of $248.1m at 31 March 2026, and Celea/Gallop transitioning to externally funded structures. Sources: FY2025 annual results, 29 April 2026, https://www.biospace.com/press-releases/puretech-announces-annual-results-for-year-ended-december-31-2025 and the company's own September 2026 corporate presentation, http://puretechhealth.com/wp-content/uploads/PRTCCorpPresentation.pdf ('248M PureTech level cash, cash equivalents as of March 31, 2026'). I mark the print slightly below that bar because today's RNS puts Gallop's external financing in 'the first half of 2027' where the April results guided 'Q1 2027', so PureTech self-funds a 100%-owned Phase 2 oncology programme for longer than the April bar implied.

findings.finding: PureTech's reaction function into this print is hostile on two independent measurements: its last three scheduled results prints returned -2.23% (FY, 2025-04-30), -5.52% (H1, 2025-08-28) and -4.15% (FY, 2026-04-29), an average of -3.97%; and on 21 September 2026, the session immediately before these interims, the company released an unambiguously positive RNS at 07:01 -- successful End-of-Phase-1 FDA meeting plus Fast Track designation for LYT-200 in relapsed/refractory high-risk MDS, on Phase 1b data showing a 27.3% complete response rate and 45.5% overall response rate -- and the shares traded to a high of 127.0p and closed at 121.0p, the low of the day, against a previous close Yahoo's intraday feed puts at 123.6p (its daily feed shows 122.6p for 18 September). A 6.4% intraday round trip, closing at the low, on good news, one session before the print. The same RNS also slipped Gallop's external financing to 'the first half of 2027' where the 29 April 2026 annual results guided 'Q1 2027', which is a plausible reason the market faded it: PureTech carries a 100%-owned Phase 2 oncology programme on its own balance sheet for longer.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: This IS the line. Five observed RNS results reactions over this stage's own window: 0.00% (Final Results 2024-04-25), +2.79% (Half-year 2024-08-28), -2.23% (Final 2025-04-30), -5.52% (Half-year 2025-08-28), -4.15% (Final 2026-04-29). Median absolute 2.79%, mean -1.82%, and monotonically worse over the last three. The single H1-specific precedent, August 2025, is the worst of the five.
findings.why_not_priced: It is not a fact about the quarter, it is a fact about how this shareholder base absorbs news, and it was generated eleven hours before this hunt. If the market were positioned for the interims to be received well, today's Fast Track RNS would not have round-tripped 6.4% and closed at the day's low on below-median volume (307,459 shares against a $1.19m/day median turnover), and the 20-day run-up would not be a thin +3.4% with a +1.84% five-day tail that today erased. The sealed lean of +1.25 says the opposite, and it is built on a short_squeeze component of +1.02 derived from a 1.70% disclosed short -- a level that cannot squeeze anything.
findings.independence: The five-print history comes from the Investegate RNS archive via the sealed baseline (https://www.investegate.co.uk/company/PRTC), a different source from today's tape and today's RNS; the free control points the same way, with a +3.4% 20-day run-up into a print this name has sold three times running. Pointing the other way: the FCA register shows shorts covering 0.20pp into the print, which is why this is sized at -2.0 and not at the -3.97% the last three prints averaged.

findings.finding: Tang Capital Management crossed to 6.07% of PureTech (14,870,983 shares) on 25 August 2026, up from 5.02%, disclosed by TR-1 RNS on 28 August 2026 -- and earlier via a 13G at 5.19% (31 March 2026 basis) and a TR-1 at 3.07% in September 2025. Tang and its vehicle Concentra Biosciences run one strategy: buy biotechs trading below the value of their cash and marketable assets and force a tender, a sale or a wind-up, having closed nine such transactions in three years for $1.2bn. PureTech is the archetype -- $248.1m of PureTech-level cash at 31 March 2026 plus 16.68m Seaport Therapeutics (Nasdaq: SPTX) shares worth ~$356m at today's $21.315, against 245,179,646 voting rights at 121.0p, a market capitalisation near $400m. The board has already written the opening: at the 29 April 2026 annual results it said it would 'look to return a greater proportion of future cash generation to shareholders, particularly in the event of any outsized returns, whilst maintaining appropriate operational runway', the AGM renewed the market-purchase authority on 10 June 2026 with 99.90% in favour, and 12,747,843 shares already sit in treasury. The interims on 22 September are the first scheduled occasion for management to answer the register.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The only precedent is the 2024 capital return: PureTech proposed a $100m tender in March 2024 at 250p, a 25% premium to the three-day VWAP, and the offer was heavily oversubscribed, buying back 31,540,670 shares. The results print that followed it, H1 on 2024-08-28, is the one positive reaction in the five-event record (+2.79%) -- the only results day in the sample on which this stock rose.
findings.why_not_priced: The disclosure channel closed in May. PureTech filed Form 25 on 11 May 2026 and 15F-12B on 21 May 2026 and has made no SEC filing since, so Tang's accumulation is now visible ONLY on the RNS -- there will be no further 13D/13G for the US shareholder base or the US-facing wires to read. Four analysts cover the name. If the market had priced a sub-NAV activist at 6%, the shares would not have drifted from 138.8p on the IPO day (1 May) to 121.0p while the Seaport stake that dominates the NAV rose from $19.84 to $21.32, and no search in either pass returned a single piece of wire or sell-side coverage of the 28 August TR-1. Sized at +1.2 rather than at the full value of a tender because the probability of it landing on THIS release is maybe one in five: the April guidance conditions a return on 'future cash generation', $70m is still earmarked for Celea, Gallop is now self-funded into H1 2027, and the Seaport shares that would fund anything larger are locked up until late October.
findings.independence: Three separate documents, none of which is the TR-1: the April 2026 capital-return sentence (https://www.biospace.com/press-releases/puretech-announces-annual-results-for-year-ended-december-31-2025), the AGM market-purchase authority and the 12.75m treasury shares (https://www.investegate.co.uk/announcement/rns/puretech-health--prtc/result-of-agm/9612206 and https://www.investegate.co.uk/announcement/rns/puretech-health--prtc/total-voting-rights/9747160), and Tang/Concentra's independently documented playbook (https://www.biopharmadive.com/news/concentra-elevation-tang-acquire-biotech-zombie-companies/750208/). It shares no document with finding 1.

outside_window.finding: Seaport Therapeutics IPO lock-up on PureTech's 16.68m SPTX shares expires 180 days after 30 April 2026, i.e. around 27 October 2026. It is the gate on any large capital return and also a supply overhang: 16.68m shares against SPTX's 126,071-share session on 2026-09-21 is roughly 130 days of that stock's volume, which is a large part of why the PureTech NAV is not realisable and the discount persists.

Gallop Oncology external financing round, to fund the Phase 2 STRIDE-MDS trial (~125 patients). Guided 'Q1 2027' at the April 2026 annual results and restated as 'the first half of 2027' in today's RNS. Until it closes, PureTech funds a 100%-owned Phase 2 programme itself.
Seaport Phase 2b BUOY-1 topline (GlyphAllo in MDD) expected H1 2027; Celea Phase 3 SURPASS-IPF topline H2 2029. These are the two events that actually re-rate the NAV and neither is in this window.

searched_and_found_nothing: The obvious NAV trade does not exist: PureTech does not track its own largest asset. Over the 95 sessions since Seaport's 1 May 2026 IPO, daily-return beta of PRTC.L to SPTX is 0.087 with correlation 0.189. SPTX fell 13.70% over the five sessions into this print (from $24.70 on 14 September to $21.315 on 21 September, a ~$56m mark-down on a ~$400m market cap) and PRTC rose 1.34% over the same sessions. I had drafted a 'catch-down' finding and the measurement killed it. No buyback is running. PureTech's RNS history carries no 'Transaction in Own Shares' announcement at all in the period reviewed, despite the AGM authority. Voting rights went UP from 243,418,190 (10 June 2026) to 245,179,646 (31 August 2026) on RSU vesting out of treasury -- the company is issuing, not repurchasing. https://www.investegate.co.uk/company/PRTC

The interim date moved from 28 August (2023, 2024 and 2025) to 22 September 2026 and I could not source a reason. The benign explanation -- the Nasdaq delisting in May 2026 removed the 6-K timetable, and the Celea asset transfer of 2 July 2026 is a complex post-balance-sheet event -- is at least as likely as anything adverse, so I put no weight on it either way.

The Cobenfy royalty is not a 2026 event: PureTech retains 2% only on annual Cobenfy net sales ABOVE $2bn, Royalty Pharma taking the rest. https://www.royaltypharma.com/news/royalty-pharma-and-puretech-health-enter-karxt-royalty-agreement/
